lines.text: `host` and `vita3k` build in parallel with anything, then wait for the machine-wide GUI lock (`scripts/gui-run.sh`, which prints who holds it), so concurrent runs from other worktrees queue instead of skewing each other. A run with no result after `VITADECK_BENCH_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 300) is killed, emulator included, and fails.

- `vita` is the source of truth. Ask Máté before running it; it is his device. It needs VitaShell's FTP server (1337) and vitacompanion (1338) running, uploads `eboot.bin`, `runtime.js`, the example Deck Apps, and any fonts or emoji the Vita lacks (the first time, about 4000 emoji take most of an hour), and leaves the Vita on the LiveArea when done. Get the IP from Máté rather than scanning for it: a bare connection such as `nc -z` crashes VitaShell's FTP and vitacompanion until the Vita restarts.

lines.text: The `upload_vita`, `upload_vpk`, and `run` targets send the build to a Vita over FTP. They need the Vita's IP in `PSVITAIP` at configure time (Compose passes it into the container), e.g. `PSVITAIP=192.168.1.177 docker compose run --rm vitasdk bash -lc "cmake -S . -B out-vita && cmake --build out-vita --target run"`. They fail with a message when it is unset.

`upload_vpk` copies the VPK to `ux0:/download/` for a manual install. `upload_vita` (and `run`) stops the running app, uploads `eboot.bin`, the runtime and the fonts, then relaunches. It also uploads `assets/emoji` (about 4,000 PNGs in one curl run), but only the first time per build directory and Vita IP and again when the images change, tracked by `out-vita/upload_emoji-<ip>.stamp`; delete that stamp to force a re-upload, e.g. after removing the app from the Vita.
